transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Ng (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (Eclipse Head of ML Ops), Priya Shah (Eclipse SRE), Evan Liu (CTO)

Summary: quick bridge to close the incident postmortem, agree on mitigations and scope a short dedicated pilot to validate long-tail latency fixes and KV cache hardening.
Topics: postmortem recap, KV cache corruption hypothesis, prefix caching and eviction behavior, dedicated vs hosted pilot options, security/SSO/KMS requirements, soak/benchmark plan, timeline and next steps.

[00:00] Lena: ok hi everyone thanks for jumping on, I know we had a rough week so this is just to align on the postmortem and the pilot scope, Marcus will go over the technical repro and safe mitigations, and then we'll discuss pilot pricing and next steps.
[00:18] Tom: yeah thanks Lena, appreciate it. quick summary from our side we had repeated p99 spikes last Tuesday, some trailing requests got really slow and that kicked off customer-facing errors, we traced it to evictions in the KV cache and then a cold KV load on the model side.
[00:34] Marcus: mm-hmm, from our tracing what we saw — and apologies if the transcription scrubs a bit — there was a race where the continuous batching + prefix cache eviction combined with a long tail of user sequences caused the GPU kernels to run longer than expected, so the default batch flush threshold didn't protect p99s.
[00:54] Priya: we also saw memory churn on the host, and I think one of our SRE alerts didn't escalate fast enough, that part is on us to tune. but the main question is if Redwood hosted would have the same behavior or if Dedicated / private infra changes that pattern.
[01:16] Marcus: good question. short answer: the pattern is workload-driven, but Dedicated gives you capacity isolation and different kernel/quantization profiles that reduce the chance of noisy neighbor evictions. however, if the prefix cache eviction logic is unchanged you'll still hit the same pathological scenario.
[01:36] Evan: does the KV cache mean like KV store in front of the model or the model's kv cache? my team uses both a prefix cache in our app and relies a bit on the model-level KV.
[01:46] Marcus: sorry I should've been clearer — two levels: client-side prefix caching and Redwood's model KV cache (the per-sequence KV for attention). both can interact. when client prefixes miss and then lots of unique prefixes flow at once, Redwood's cache fills and evicts older entries. eviction causes re-computation and heavy GPU work.
[02:08] Tom: so root cause hypothesis is workload variance + non-optimal eviction policy + batch flush thresholds set for average latency not tail.
[02:20] Marcus: yup. also our kernel selection heuristics picked a slower attention kernel for some sequence shapes under that load; that was surfaced in the perf profile. again this is patchable in the runtime but we need a reproducible test.
[02:36] Priya: can you reproduce in a staging sim? our concern is that in prod it's intermittent and tied to peak bursts.
[02:44] Marcus: we believe so. Marcus: we created a small repro that roughly simulates your traffic distribution — it ramps a lot of unique short prefixes then a few long sequences. we'll run a 48-hour soak in Eclipse staging to see tail behavior and capture evictions, kv cache watermarks, and GPU kernel switches.
[03:06] Lena: thanks. on the mitigation side we recommended three levers: change eviction policy to favor hot prefixes, tune continuous batching thresholds (lower flush size on high concurrency), and optionally pin a Dedicated pool for the pilot to isolate capacity.
[03:24] Tom: pinning Dedicated sounds good, but we need to know the unit economics and SLA.
[03:30] Lena: understood — I'll send Dedicated pilot pricing and a small SLA table after this call. also there is a smaller change we can push that doesn't require Dedicated: runtime patch to change the eviction favoring and back-off heuristics — that would be a configuration flip for hosted customers.
[03:48] Evan: that sounds promising. what about encryption and our KMS? we need to keep keys in our HSM, and audit logs for model inputs for compliance.
[03:56] Marcus: Redwood Private or Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via HSM integration, and we export audit logs. we'll attach SOC2 evidence and the architecture diagram.
[04:12] Priya: one more question, how intrusive is the runtime patch? does it risk regression on token cost?
[04:18] Marcus: minimal. the eviction tweak biases toward cache hits, might slightly increase memory use but should reduce recompute and net tokens generated — we'd expect token unit cost to go down on average because less re-computation. we'll measure during the soak.
[04:34] Tom: ok can you outline the soak plan? we need to know observability hooks so our SREs can watch the right metrics.
[04:42] Marcus: plan: 48-hour soak in your staging cluster with a mirrored traffic generator. We'll capture: KV cache size/watermarks per pod, eviction counts, batch size distributions, per-kernel execution times, GPU utilization, request latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), and trace IDs for slow traces. We'll push debug telemetry to a secure bucket and provide a sanitized report.
[05:08] Priya: what about retention for those traces — we can't share PII.
[05:12] Lena: agreed — we'll do sanitized traces and we can sign a one-off NDA if needed; also we can run the soak in your VPC if you want private deployment.
[05:24] Evan: timeline wise we want the pilot in the next two weeks — is that realistic?
[05:30] Lena: yes if we get access to staging traffic and a quick contract, we can start within 10 business days.
[05:36] Tom: procurement may need 2-3 weeks, but we can start staging setup and the soak once Redwood shares the test harness.
[05:44] Marcus: for the test harness we'll send a traffic generator script and example config for prefix distributions. small heads-up: the script uses gRPC and the header fields are slightly different 'cause of our SDK.
[05:58] Priya: also we profiled memory churn and we'd like to test a runtime build with a patch that improves memory reuse for KV pages. is that something Redwood can provide as a canary build?
[06:10] Marcus: yes we can spin a canary runtime with the memory reuse patch; it'll require a short maintenance window to swap images in staging. low risk.
[06:20] Evan: perfect. let's talk about acceptance criteria for the pilot — what success looks like.
[06:26] Lena: initial acceptance criteria proposal: reduce P99 tail to below your target (you said 250ms), no correlated increase in total token cost > 10%, and no more than X error spikes over the 48-hour run. also capture whether Dedicated pinning materially reduces variance.
[06:44] Tom: 250ms at p99 is aggressive but that's our SLO. we'll share historical numbers; currently we hit ~420ms on bad days.
[06:52] Marcus: ok we'll measure pre/post and provide delta.
[06:56] Priya: security checklist — SSO, SAML, audit logs, data residency (EU only for some customers) and KMS/HSM, plus PCI-ish constraints for payment data, though not all traffic touches payments.
[07:14] Lena: noted — Marcus will include the security pack; we'll attach SOC2, ISO docs and network diag.
[07:20] Evan: are there any competitors we should be concerned about?
[07:24] Tom: we looked at InferentiaX for a dedicated box and CloudAI for a managed endpoint, plus some internal build options. cost and operator effort are the main concerns.
[07:36] Marcus: fair. our advantage is the runtime optimizations and the ability to roll a hotfix without a full infra change. but we'll show hard numbers.
[07:44] Lena: ok let's recap next steps: Redwood runs a 48-hour soak in staging, provide canary runtime with eviction/memory patches, send Dedicated pilot pricing, and provide security/compliance artifacts. Eclipse provides traffic profile, procurement timeline, and staging access.
[08:04] Tom: agreed. anything else on mitigation roadmap?
[08:08] Marcus: long term we'll propose a fallback orchestration policy: graceful degrade to a cheaper quantized model variant for long-tail requests and circuit-break on extreme KV churn. that's a Q1 roadmap item.
[08:22] Priya: that sounds like the right approach.
[08:24] Lena: perfect. we'll follow up with an email and put calendar hold for a 12/08 follow-up to review soak.

[08:36] -- timestamps in body are approximate and speakers talk over each other sometimes; some words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache, "quantized" could be "quant eyesed").

End of transcript.
